text:
zoe: Noticed multiple downstream sample apps failing after we changed package exports last night. Errors show up in Vercel Edge and Node bundlers differently.

marcus: quick log from a user: `Error: Cannot find module '@redwood/inference-js/lib/auth'` when they do a deep import. Previously supported.

abby: We tightened exports to only `.` and `./runtime` to encourage unified consumer surface, but that blocked subpath imports and also hid types for some TS resolvers.

zoe: Also saw a cloud preview with `fetch is not defined` inside our auth retry; suspect bundler chose a server-only variant because edge conditional fields missing.

marcus: Proposed fix: restore explicit conditional exports for `import`/`require` and add subpath exports for `./auth` and `./adapters/*`. Add `./package.json` to exports and set top-level `types` to `dist/index.d.ts`.

abby: agree. Also add `typesVersions` fallback for older TS so declaration files resolve when exports map hides .d.ts paths.

pkg-bot: CI: created branch fix/exportmap-restore, build started.

zoe: Small runtime change too: replace strict `if (typeof fetch !== 'function') throw` with `const _fetch = globalThis.fetch ?? (() => require('node-fetch'))()` lazy fallback. Keeps edge polyfills intact.

marcus: I'll prepare a patch and a beta release so we can test on samples runner. Also update release checklist to include Deno/edge smoke tests and deep-import verification.

abby: Add short note in docs: "Prefer top-level import; deep imports supported for compatibility. If you see import resolution errors, pin to last working patch until we release fix."

pkg-bot: CI green on fix/exportmap-restore. Publishing 1.4.1-beta.1.

zoe: Verified sample apps on Vercel dev and Node repros. Closing for now, will monitor errors.
